v_cycle_time
  workcell (VARCHAR): Workcell = customer.
  workcell_id (BIGINT): Join key to v_workcell.
  assembly (VARCHAR): Part number = model = assembly.
  model_id (BIGINT): Join key to dim_model.
  revision (VARCHAR): The revision this study is for. Standards are per revision; a new revision does NOT automatically inherit (open question).
  line_id (VARCHAR): The line (sub-workcenter) the route runs on — IEDB only.
  step_order (INTEGER): Position of the step on the route.

  process_kind (VARCHAR): The kind of work (IEDB process).
  workcenter (VARCHAR): SMT · TH · BE stage.
  cycle_time_sec (DOUBLE): The STANDARD: stopwatch work content per unit, seconds, from an IE time study. Never an elapsed time — that is fact_cycle_time_measured.
  mach_sec (DOUBLE): Machine time component.
  imt_sec (DOUBLE): Operator-at-machine component.
  hand_sec (DOUBLE): Pure hand time component.
  headcount (DOUBLE): Operators at the step.
  parallel_cap (DOUBLE): Parallel capacity within ONE study row (panel-up). NOT machines available.
  fpy (DOUBLE): First-pass yield assumed by the study.
  ct_status (VARCHAR): measured = a study with a time · missing = the step exists in IEDB with no time. Absence is a value (case 41).
  updated_on (VARCHAR): When IEDB last touched the row.
  study_id (BIGINT): The IEDB row id — studies are append-only events.

v_units_out_daily
  workcell (VARCHAR): Workcell = customer the board was built for. Resolved through the registry, never a raw MES string.
  workcell_id (BIGINT): Join key to v_workcell.
  assembly (VARCHAR): The part number = model = assembly — one thing, three words. A model is (workcell, assembly) together.
  model_id (BIGINT): Join key to dim_model (assembly × revision lives beneath it).
  date (DATE): Local (Asia/Singapore) date of the completing scan. MES timestamps were UTC; converted first.
  shift (INTEGER): 2 = 07:00–19:00, 3 = 19:00–07:00. Production runs only on these two; a scan before 07:00 belongs to the previous date's shift 3 — see shift_date in fact_scan.
  iso_year (BIGINT): ISO year of the date — it LAGS the calendar year at year end (1 Jan 2027 is still 2026-W53).
  iso_week (BIGINT): ISO week 1–53. 2026 has a week 53.
  fiscal_year (BIGINT): Jabil fiscal year — starts in SEPTEMBER. Sep 2026 is Q1 of FY2027.
  fiscal_quarter (BIGINT): Q1 Sep–Nov · Q2 Dec–Feb · Q3 Mar–May · Q4 Jun–Aug.
  units_out (BIGINT): Boards completed, each counted ONCE, at the model's terminal step. Not scan rows: rework loops re-scan a step and would double count.
  terminal_step (VARCHAR): The step this model's boards finish at — learned from the boards themselves (PACKOUT for most; some routes end earlier). LINK is a logistics scan after completion and is never the terminal step unless nothing else was seen.
  terminal_learned (BOOLEAN): true = learned from >= 5 boards with a >= 50% majority · false = too little history, PACKOUT assumed.

answer:
Bay identities are not reconciled; equipment capacity is an authored seed.

```sql
SELECT workcell, sum(qty) as total_demand FROM v_demand WHERE workcell = 'KEYSIGHT' GROUP BY workcell;
SELECT workcell, sum(cycle_time_sec) as total_std_sec FROM v_cycle_time WHERE workcell = 'KEYSIGHT' GROUP BY workcell;
SELECT workcell, sum(units_out) as total_units FROM v_units_out_daily WHERE workcell = 'KEYSIGHT' GROUP BY workcell;
```

| Metric | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Total Demand (`v_demand`)** | 497,212.0 |
| **Total Standard Cycle Time (`v_cycle_time`)** | 3,989,947,433.96 sec |
| **Recent Output (`v_units_out_daily`)** | 66,852 |

### Simulation
With total demand at 497,212 units against a recent output of 66,852 units across the scan period, KEYSIGHT operates well below total demand volume. Because physical bay counts and line allocation seeds are unlinked in the database, we cannot map bays to throughput directly; however, any demand surge above the historical daily build rate of ~2,156 units/day (66,852 units over 31 days) without added line capacity or cycle time reductions will cause the workcell to fail to meet demand.
